title: Engine Fuel — Fuel Metering Unit — Install the Revised Delivery Nozzle and Relocate the Cowl Latch Bracket
abstract: Installs the revised fuel metering unit delivery nozzle that holds its spray pattern at low fuel temperature, and moves the cowl latch bracket outboard to restore clearance to the nozzle shroud.

sections.planning_reason: Cold soak starts on the higher rated installation showed a longer light-up time and a wide spread between engines, traced to the delivery nozzle spray pattern collapsing below minus twenty degrees. During the same investigation twelve aircraft were found with witness marks between the cowl latch and the nozzle shroud, caused by a stack-up present only on this installation. Both are corrected here so that the engine is opened once.
sections.description: This bulletin replaces the delivery nozzle with the revised item carrying the new swirl insert and a two millimetre shorter body, and replaces the cowl latch bracket with the variant that moves the latch six millimetres outboard. The nozzle shroud, the mount link and the fuel feed connection are unchanged, so no engine build standard change is required.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Open the fan cowl and make the engine safe for fuel system work, then drain the metering unit to the collection point. Disconnect and remove the existing delivery nozzle following AMM-M-73-10-11-000-046-A and cap the open connections immediately. Install the revised nozzle with new seals and torque to the value in the bulletin, then remove the cowl latch bracket and install the relocated bracket on the existing holes. Measure the clearance between the latch and the nozzle shroud at the closed position and confirm twelve millimetres minimum. Restore the fuel system, do a leak check at idle and a functional start check, then close the cowl and make the records entry. Repeat for the second engine.
sections.effectivity_note: Applies to MERIDIAN-46 aircraft with the higher rated installation delivered before MSN M00401. Both engines must be embodied within one hundred flight hours of each other, so that the start behaviour is symmetric and the crew is not comparing two standards.
sections.material_note: Kit is per engine and contains the delivery nozzle, the cowl latch bracket, the seal set and the capping plugs. The removed nozzle is returned for teardown within sixty days; the removed bracket is scrapped locally.

type_data.compliance_time: Within 30 months of the date of this Service Bulletin, or before the next cold season for operators north of 55 degrees.
